zone: Carriers price by 'zone' — a number (2-8 in this model) representing how far the destination is from the origin. Higher zone = farther = more expensive. Zone 2 is nearby, Zone 8 is coast-to-coast/farthest.
fuel_surcharge: A variable percentage carriers add to the base transportation charge to account for fuel cost fluctuations. Changes weekly/monthly in the real world; this prototype uses a fixed illustrative rate.
residential_delivery: A flat surcharge carriers add when delivering to a home address instead of a commercial business address, because residential routes cost more to service.
saturday_delivery: An accessorial fee for requesting delivery (or pickup) on a Saturday. Only available on certain expedited services — not standard Ground in this model — and must be requested at shipment creation.
dim_weight: Dimensional (DIM) weight approximates density: (Length x Width x Height in inches) / 139. Carriers bill whichever is greater — the actual scale weight or the DIM weight — so large-but-light packages (e.g. a lampshade) can cost much more than their scale weight suggests.
additional_handling: A surcharge for packages that are hard to mechanically sort: oversized dimensions, over a weight threshold, or irregular/non-rigid packaging (e.g. a package wrapped in plastic, a tube, a tire).
oversize: A steeper surcharge (beyond additional handling) for packages exceeding a length-plus-girth threshold. Oversize packages are also billed a minimum billable weight regardless of actual weight.
delivery_area_surcharge: DAS/EDAS ('extended DAS') — a surcharge for delivering to ZIP codes the carrier has classified as remote or costly to serve, on top of the normal zone-based rate.
signature_required: A surcharge to require a signature on delivery instead of leaving the package unattended.
address_correction: A fee charged after pickup if the carrier's system flags and corrects an inaccurate address you provided. Not knowable before shipping, so it never appears on a pre-shipment quote.
peak_season_surcharge: A temporary surcharge carriers add during the high-volume holiday shipping window (roughly mid-October through mid-January) on top of normal rates.
billable_weight: The weight a carrier actually charges for — the greater of the package's actual (scale) weight and its dimensional (DIM) weight.
general_rate_increase: GRI — the annual across-the-board rate increase (typically effective each January) that UPS and FedEx apply to published list rates.
